Question_text: SSG manufactures mobile (cell) phones using batch production. Quality control is important. SSG has 130 employees who all receive on-the-job training. The Marketing Manager is analysing cost and output data for product X. An extract is shown in Table 1.1. As product X is in the maturity stage of the product life cycle SSG is considering possible extension strategies.
image: Table 1.1 shows cost and output data for product X. It includes Rent and other expenses per month at $300,000, Variable cost per unit at $80, and Output per month at 12,000 units.
Sub_topic: Features, benefits, limitations: job, batch, flow production
Benefits, limitations: induction, on-the-job, off-the-job training
Classify costs: fixed, variable, average, total
Product life cycle: stages, extension strategies

Parts.part_text: Define 'on-the-job training'.
Calculate total variable cost per month. Show your working.
Identify four factors a business should consider when deciding which method of production to use.
Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to SSG of using quality control.
Do you think adding new features to a product is the best extension strategy for a manufacturing business to use? Justify your answer.

Question_text: DNG provides electricity to 16 million customers. It is a limited company which means DNG's shareholders benefit from limited liability. DNG is planning to stop using coal to produce its electricity. Pressure groups had an influence on this decision. The Managing Director knows there will be an opportunity cost to making this change. She is considering the best way to communicate this important information to DNG's 6500 employees.
Sub_topic: Concepts of needs, wants, scarcity, opportunity cost
Methods of measuring size: employees, output, capital employed
Benefits, limitations of methods, including IT

Parts.part_text: Define 'opportunity cost'.
Identify two limitations of using the number of employees to measure the size of a business.
Outline how having limited liability might benefit DNG's shareholders.
Explain two ways a pressure group might influence DNG's decisions.
Explain two methods of internal communication a large business could use to share important information with its employees. Justify which method should be used.

Having the right marketing mix is important to CPK's success. The Finance Director is analysing CPK's financial statements. An extract is shown in Table 3.1. He wants to know how an increase in taxation might affect CPK's business.

Sub_topic: Importance of marketing mix elements in decisions
Ratios: gross profit margin, profit margin, return on capital employed, current ratio, acid test ratio
Non-financial: job enrichment, rotation, teamworking, training, promotion
Financial rewards: wage, salary, bonus, commission, profit sharing

Parts.part_text: Define 'non-current assets'.
State two elements of the marketing mix.

Question_text: Following the end of a recession in country X, Beena wants to start up a hairdressing business. One option is to purchase a franchise from an established hairdressing business. Beena has $800 in savings and knows having enough working capital will be important for her business. She plans to use market research to help her decision-making. Beena knows there are many ways to segment a market.
Sub_topic: Stages of business cycle: growth, boom, recession, slump
How/why segment: age, socio-economic, location, gender
Features: sole traders, partnerships, private/public limited companies, franchises, joint ventures

Parts.part_text: Define 'recession'.
Identify two ways of segmenting a market.
Outline two reasons why having enough working capital might be important for Beena's business.
Explain two possible advantages to Beena of buying a franchise.
Do you think it is always better for a start-up business to use primary market research, rather than secondary market research, when making decisions? Justify your answer.
